newsitem.title: USA: Phillips to build a methyl mercaptan plant.
newsitem.headline: Phillips to build a methyl mercaptan plant.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said on Thursday that its board has approved the construction of a 100 million-pounds-per-year methyl mercaptan facility at the company's Borger, Texas, Complex.
"The new facility will mark Phillips' entry into the methyl mercaptan business and expand our already extensive mercaptan product line," said Guy Sutherland, vice president, chemicals.
Methyl mercaptan is a sulfur-based chemical used in the production of methionine, a feed supplement for poultry. It also is a key ingrediant in agricultural chemicals.
Phillips said it plans to sell methyl mercaptan to the merchant market and to Novus International Inc, a major producer of methionine. Novus is owned by Mitsui & Co Ltd and Nippon Soda Co Ltd.
Construction is expected to begin late in 1996, with first production scheduled for the fourth quarter of 1998, Phillips said. The cost of the project was not disclosed.

It said the facility also will produce dimethyl sulfide (DMS), dimethyl disulfide (DMDS), methane sulfonic acid (MSA) and methane sulfonyl chloride (MSC). These are sulfur chemicals widely used in petrochemical, agricultural, electronic and other applications.
